papers.title: Versatile Biodegradable Poly(acrylic acid)-Based Hydrogels Infiltrated in Porous Titanium Implants to Improve the Biofunctional Performance.
papers.abstract: This research work proposes a synergistic approach to improve implants' performance through the use of porous Ti substrates to reduce the mismatch between Young's modulus of Ti (around 110 GPa) and the cortical bone (20-25 GPa), and the application of a biodegradable, acrylic acid-based polymeric coating to reduce bacterial adhesion and proliferation, and to enhance osseointegration. First, porous commercially pure Ti substrates with different porosities and pore size distributions were fabricated by using space-holder techniques to obtain substrates with improved tribomechanical behavior. On the other hand, a new diacrylate cross-linker containing a reduction-sensitive disulfide bond was synthesized to prepare biodegradable poly(acrylic acid)-based hydrogels with 1, 2, and 4% cross-linker. Finally, after the required characterization, both strategies were implemented, and the combination of 4% cross-linked poly(acrylic acid)-based hydrogel infiltrated in 30 vol % porosity, 100-200 μm average pore size, was revealed as an outstanding choice for enhancing implant performance.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文使用了多孔钛基底降低刚度不匹配并涂覆生物可降解水凝胶，但未采用LPBF制造且未评估疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: Does not involve LPBF fabrication, does not report fatigue testing, and lacks detailed characterization of as-built surface morphology.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过多孔钛和水凝胶涂层协同改善植入物的力学与生物性能。
summary_zh.method: 采用空间占位法制备多孔钛基底并合成含双硫键的可降解水凝胶涂层。
summary_zh.result: 含4%交联剂的涂层和多孔钛（30%孔隙率，100-200 μm孔径）组合性能最佳。
summary_zh.validation: 对钛基底进行摩擦力学测试，对水凝胶进行降解和力学表征。

summary_en.motivation: To reduce the Young's modulus mismatch between titanium implants and bone while enhancing biofunctionality via a biodegradable polymeric coating.
summary_en.method: Porous titanium substrates were fabricated using space-holder techniques, and biodegradable poly(acrylic acid)-based hydrogels with a reduction-sensitive cross-linker were synthesized and infiltrated into the pores.
summary_en.result: The combination of 4% cross-linked hydrogel and 30% porosity titanium with 100-200 μm pores showed optimal tribomechanical and biofunctional performance.
summary_en.validation: Substrates were characterized for tribomechanical properties, and hydrogels for degradation and mechanical behavior.
